subject: Post-demo: StratusIQ inference comparison checklist & gating tests

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo: StratusIQ inference comparison checklist & gating tests

Elena —

Thanks again for the demo today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get an apples-to-apples comparison against the hyperscalers you mentioned:

Summary (what we heard)
- Primary goals: reduce inference cost while keeping latency under 120ms p95 for serving UI flows; lower hallucination rate on entity extraction prompts; predictable throughput for bulk batch jobs.
- Existing constraints: data residency in us-west; test dataset ~10k conversation turns; procurement timeline ~Q4.

Redwood differentiators we demonstrated
- Prefix/KV caching that preserves p95 latency under mixed workloads
- Configurable quantization profiles with measurable quality deltas
- Smart routing for cheaper model variants when latency budget allows

Proposed gating tests (short list) — we can run these on Hosted API or provide config for you to run in your environment:
1) Latency profile: p50/p95/p99 for short (32 tokens), medium (128), and long (512) contexts — stable load at 50 req/s.
2) Hallucination probe suite: 500 targeted prompts (entity-laden + instruction-following) to measure hallucination_rate and answer_precision.
3) Cost/throughput: token-level cost model across quantized vs fp16 variants for a 1M-token simulated month.
4) Regression checks: run the same probe set against your current hyperscaler baseline (we can supply a baseline_results_template).

Attachments: I’ve attached a starter evaluation matrix and a set of probe prompts (CSV/TXT stubs) to make this reproducible.

Asks from StratusIQ
- Share the 10k test dataset (or a sample) and the expected QPS pattern.
- Confirm which hyperscaler(s) you want us to compare against (AWS Bedrock, GCP Vertex, or your in-house infra).
- Approve a 1-hour follow-up to run through the probe matrix and hand off the test harness (I have Monday morning open).

Next steps:
- Elena: please upload a sample dataset or confirm access method.
- Ben/Marissa: review the attached probes and suggest any domain-specific prompts we should add (finance / legal / product Q&A).
- Jordan: schedule follow-up once we have dataset access.

Thanks — Jordan

Elena / team —

Thanks — adding more concrete test definitions so the eval can be automated and comparable across providers. Posting the core probe prompts inline and attached as stratus_probe_prompts.txt.

Quick runbook (recommended):
- Environment: run three columns: Redwood hosted (default model), GCP Vertex (matched model size), AWS (matched model size). Keep identical prompt set and seed where applicable.
- Sequence lengths: 32 / 128 / 512 (mix 70/25/5 split)
- Load pattern: steady 50 rps for 15 minutes per run, then a 5-minute spike to 200 rps to test p99 behavior.
- Metrics: latency_p50/p95/p99 (ms), hallucination_rate (%) using yes/no oracle for factuality, answer_precision (F1 for NER/extraction tasks), tokens_per_request, cost_estimate_per_1m_tokens.

Suggested gating thresholds (can be tuned):
- latency_p95 <= 120ms (UI flows)
- hallucination_rate <= 3% on the probe set
- answer_precision >= 0.88 for entity extraction tasks

Probe examples (excerpt):
- "Extract the company name and revenue figure from this paragraph: ..."
- "Was any personal data mentioned in the following chat? If yes, list types."
- "Given the short user query, provide a single-sentence factual summary and cite the source if present."

Attachments shipped: redwood_eval_matrix.csv (templates for results), stratus_probe_prompts.txt (500 probes), baseline_results_template.xlsx (results upload).

Notes on quantization & Dedicated/private runs:
- Quantized variants (4/8-bit) are available as drop-in model checkpoints for Redwood Dedicated — no kernel rebuild required for standard linux GPU stacks we ship. If you deploy on an unusual accelerator or very old CUDA, our engineering team can provide a compatibility matrix.
- Audit logs retention: we retain token-level logs for 30 days by default in Hosted; Dedicated/Private gives you control over retention and KMS integrations (SOC2 documentation set linked below).

Link: https://redwood.ai/compliance/soc2-summary.pdf
